implementation_notes: Foundation's NotificationCenter is the platform bus: post a named Notification with a userInfo dictionary, subscribe with addObserver(forName:object:queue:using:) or the newer typed NotificationCenter.Message API, and remove the returned token or the observer in deinit. The event is the Notification plus a stringly-typed name, so keep the names in one place and build the userInfo payload in a factory per event; the typed message API (iOS 26 and later) removes the string and dictionary coupling.
pitfalls: Block-based observers are retained by the center: forgetting to remove the token leaks the closure and keeps it firing after its owner is gone; prefer the typed message observers or the notifications(named:object:) async sequence in new code.
userInfo is an untyped dictionary: a renamed key still compiles and silently yields nil at the receiver.

variants.name: Combine PassthroughSubject event bus
variants.idiom_name: PassthroughSubject<DomainEvent, Never> + compactMap type filter + AnyCancellable
variants.implementation_notes: Combine gives a typed, composable bus: a PassthroughSubject<DomainEvent, Never> (or one subject per event type) is the publisher, eraseToAnyPublisher() exposes it read-only, subscribers filter with compactMap { $0 as? OrderPlaced }, delivery threads are explicit with receive(on:), and lifetime is managed by AnyCancellable. A subject drops values when nobody subscribes, so it is a signal bus rather than a durable log. Requires Swift 5.1 / the Combine framework (Apple platforms).
pitfalls: Values sent before a subscription exists are dropped; for events that must not be missed, hold state or use a replaying subject or buffer.
Every subscription must keep its AnyCancellable alive: a cancellable dropped inside a function silently unsubscribes.

variants.name: AsyncStream continuation fan-out
variants.idiom_name: actor holding [UUID: AsyncStream<DomainEvent>.Continuation] + for await consumption
variants.implementation_notes: With structured concurrency the bus is an AsyncStream: the publisher keeps one continuation per consumer and yields each event to them, consumers iterate with for await inside a Task, and cancellation runs onTermination, which is where the continuation is removed. Because continuations and the registry are mutable shared state, the bus belongs in an actor, which also serializes emission. Requires Swift 5.5 or later; choose it over Combine when the app is already async/await and the reactive operator set is not needed.
pitfalls: AsyncStream does not buffer in this design: events yielded while a consumer is not yet iterating are lost, so consumers must start before publication or the stream needs an explicit buffering policy.
A continuation kept in a dictionary keeps the consumer's stream alive; removing it only in onTermination means a consumer that never cancels leaks.
